title: Appealing a Decline Due to Alternative Income Source Detection
description: What to do when SASSA declines your grant saying you have an alternative income source but the deposits in your account are not actual income. Sworn affidavit and appeal strategy.

contentBlocks.title: Appealing a Decline Due to Alternative Income Source Detection
contentBlocks.description: SASSA's automated bank audit can flag deposits in your account as alternative income. If those deposits are gifts, loans, or savings transfers, this guide shows you how to prepare a sworn affidavit and submit a successful appeal.

contentBlocks.text: Appealing a Decline Due to Alternative Income Source Detection

One of the most common SRD decline reasons is 'Alternative Income Source Detected'. This happens when SASSA's automated bank audit finds deposits in your account. If these deposits are not actual income, you need a specific appeal strategy.
This guide is for SRD R370 grant applicants whose status shows 'Alternative Income Source Detected' because of bank account deposits.

steps.title: Review your bank statements
steps.description: Review your bank statements for the months in question and identify all deposits.

steps.title: Explain each deposit
steps.description: For each deposit, prepare an explanation (gift from family, loan repayment, savings transfer).

steps.title: Write a sworn affidavit
steps.description: Write a sworn affidavit at your nearest SAPS station explaining the nature of each deposit.

steps.title: Submit your appeal
steps.description: Submit your appeal on the ITSAA portal and upload the affidavit and bank statements.

steps.title: Select the right option
steps.description: Tick the option that says 'Deposits are not income — they are gifts/loans/savings'.

contentBlocks.title: Timeline
contentBlocks.text: File within 90 days. Each month is treated separately — you must appeal each declined month individually.

items: Bank statements showing the deposits that triggered the decline
Sworn affidavit explaining each deposit (commissioned by SAPS)
Proof of your current unemployment status (if applicable)
Supporting letters from family members if deposits were gifts

faqs.question: My friend sent me R500 as a birthday gift. Will SASSA count this as income?
faqs.answer: Yes, any deposit into your account can trigger the 'Alternative Income Source' flag. You can appeal by providing a sworn statement from your friend confirming it was a gift.

faqs.question: How much money in deposits can trigger this status?
faqs.answer: Any single deposit over R624 (the SRD threshold) can trigger the flag. Multiple smaller deposits totalling over R624 can also trigger it.
